The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953076;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #953076;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953076;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953076;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #953076;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953076;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8e490b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1461a3;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1461a3;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1461a3;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #953076;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #953076;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #953076;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e490b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; MC	<p>f482_fb58</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8e490b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e490b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #566600;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #566600;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #566600;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e490b;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e490b;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1e6974;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1e6974;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0a6789;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0a6789;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #82399a;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #82399a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #82399a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7d550c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d550c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1461a3;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1461a3;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1461a3;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f351f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f351f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #683fbd;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #683fbd;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6c5e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6c5e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #276f24;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #276f24;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f24;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4154b4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4154b4;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9e2f4c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e2f4c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
